text.p: NAIROBI, August 13 (Reuter) These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Ford Asili Chairman, Kenneth Matiba says public input should ttbe used in Kenya's constitutional reform process.
World Bank official says bank will not disburse $71.6 million (5 billion shillings) structural adjustment credit to Kenya until several conditions are met.
President Moi says he will soon announce the election date and asked Kenyans to get ready.
Ford Asili chairman, Kenneth Matiba has proposed that an international technical team of experts be invited to facilitate the constitutional reform process.
The driver of Ford Kenya MP for Mathare, Ochieng Mbeo arrested outside parliament buildings in connection with the murder of a policeman in Nairobi on Aug 8.
Assistant Minister Julius Sunkuli says Richard Leakey, a former Director of the Kenya Widlife Services, used the organization's funds to set up the unregistered Safina party.
United States Ambassador to Kenya, Prudence Bushnell, takes swipe at political parties in the country for derailing the constitutional reform dialogue.
Ford Kenya Chairman, Wamalwa Kijana, said over the weekend he fell out with National Convention Executive Council when he realized it had been hijacked by leaders of Safina.
KANU Secretary General Joseph Kamotho rejects calls for a constitutional conference as opposed to the already instituted dialogue.
